text_en: Naeem Aslam, Chief Investment Officer at London-based Zaye Capital Markets, said that from an operational perspective, the details of Europe's agreement to release diesel stocks are "very rough." The announcement appears intended to ease pressure, but the actual structural changes, namely who will release these stocks and where the bans will be lifted, remain unclear. This decision is merely an attempt to "slow the bleeding" and will have an adverse impact on the market. Imagine a bank run occurs in the market, and suddenly the central bank steps in and says you can only withdraw a certain amount from banks. This does indeed slow the bleeding process, but it also creates more volatility in specific aspects of investor confidence in these institutions. Now, this logic applies perfectly to the news that Europe will release diesel reserves.
